short: One of the US Navy's first aircraft carriers, USS Lexington was lost during the Battle of the Coral Sea in 1942.
full:
Commissioned in 1927 alongside her sister ship Saratoga, USS Lexington was originally designed as a massive battlecruiser before being converted to an aircraft carrier under the Washington Naval Treaty. Known as "Lady Lex", she played a fundamental role in developing American carrier tactics during the interwar period. Her air groups provided crucial defense and striking power in the chaotic early months of the Pacific War.

In May 1942, Lexington participated in the Battle of the Coral Sea, the first naval engagement in history where opposing ships never sighted one another. After helping sink the Japanese light carrier Shoho, she was struck by multiple torpedoes and bombs from Japanese aircraft. Uncontrollable fuel vapor fires forced her crew to abandon ship, and she was scuttled by an escorting destroyer.
